title: Austria — HCCH 1961 competent authorities (world index, needs review)

authorities.name: The Federal Ministry for Europe, Integration and Foreign Affairs
authorities.source_name: The Federal Ministry for Europe, Integration and Foreign Affairs with regard to all documents issued by:

authorities.name: the Federal President or the Office of the Federal President,
the President of the National Council, the President of the Federal Council or the Parliamentary Administrative Office,
the federal government,
a federal ministry,
the Constitutional Court or the Administrative Court,
the Supreme Court, the Supreme Cartel Court at the Supreme Court, the Supreme Restoration Commission at the Supreme Court, the Supreme Restitution Commission at the Supreme Court or
the Court of Audit.
Austrian Embassies and Consulates (except for Honorary-General-Consulates)
authorities.source_name: The following documents can be issued by Austrian Embassies and Consulates (except for Honorary-General-Consulates) and provided with an Apostille:

authorities.name: Civil status documents and register extracts
Certificates of no impediment
Certificates of the ability to establish a registered partnership
Proof of citizenship
Certificates of exit from the State
Criminal records
The presidents of civil courts of first instance
authorities.source_name: The presidents of civil courts of first instance, or their designated representatives for the issue of certificates (apostilles), with the exception of the Commercial Court in Vienna and the Juvenile Court in Vienna, with regard to all documents issued in the region served by the court in question by:

authorities.name: a court other than those referred to in point 1 (e) and (f),
a public prosecutor's office,
a notary,
a chamber of notaries or a bar association, in so far as the chamber or association in question did so in the execution of official federal duties.
With regard to all other documents,
Provincial governments
authorities.source_name: provincial governments, for documents issued in their province in the execution of official federal duties.
